Sum over the predation kernel

Source: R/setPredKernel.R
convolve_pred_kernel.Rd

Evaluates the sums over the predation kernel that underlie the encounter rate, the predation rate and the predation diffusion, using the Fourier-transformed kernels that setPredKernel() stores in the MizerParams object. This is how mizerEncounter(), mizerPredRate(), mizerDiffusion() and getDiet() evaluate these sums. An extension package that needs such a sum for a density of its own should call this function rather than multiplying the Fourier-transformed kernels itself, so that it does not depend on how mizer stores them.

Usage

convolve_pred_kernel(
  params,
  x,
  kernel = c("encounter", "predation", "diffusion")
)

Arguments

params

A MizerParams object. For a partially overridden kernel, explicit sums are used for the overridden species and Fourier convolutions for the others. A wholly custom kernel set with setPredKernel() is not supported by this helper.

x

For kernel = "encounter" or "diffusion", a matrix (species x size in w_full(params)) of prey densities, or a vector with one entry per size in w_full(params) that is used for every species. For kernel = "predation", a matrix (species x size in w(params)) of predator densities, or a vector with one entry per size in w(params).

kernel

Which sum to evaluate: "encounter" (the default), "predation" or "diffusion".

Value

A matrix (species x predator size in w(params)) for kernel = "encounter" or "diffusion", and a matrix (species x prey size in w_full(params)) for kernel = "predation".

Details

With kernel = "encounter" the result is $$\sum_{k} \phi_i(w_j, w_k)\, x_{ik}$$ for each species \(i\) and each predator size \(w_j\) in w(params), where the sum runs over the prey sizes \(w_k\) in w_full(params). With kernel = "diffusion" the same sum is evaluated with the kernel used for the predation diffusion, which differs from the encounter kernel only when bin averaging is switched on (see second_order_w()). With kernel = "predation" the result is $$\sum_{j} \phi_i(w_j, w_k)\, x_{ij}$$ for each species \(i\) and each prey size \(w_k\) in w_full(params), where the sum runs over the predator sizes \(w_j\) in w(params).

The entries of x are the summands without the kernel, so they include the size-bin widths: for the encounter rate, for example, x is the prey biomass density times dw_full(params). Pair them with the plain point weights, not with bin-averaged ones, even when bin averaging is switched on; see encounter_kernel() for why.

The sums are evaluated as convolutions by fast Fourier transform. For a model of defaults edition 3 or later (see defaults_edition()) they only run over sizes on the grid: the part of a kernel that extends below the smallest size in w_full(params) contributes nothing. This is achieved by evaluating the convolutions on a zero-padded grid, so that the part of a kernel that falls off one end of the grid does not wrap around to pick up the densities at the other end. A model of an earlier edition keeps the circular convolutions of earlier versions of mizer, so that its results do not change. In such a model, the part of the kernel of a small predator that extends below the smallest size in w_full(params) wraps around to the largest sizes, so that the smallest predators are credited with eating the largest prey.

See also

encounter_kernel(), pred_kernel()

Examples

params <- NS_params
# The rate at which each predator encounters resource biomass, per unit
# search volume
prey <- initialNResource(params) * w_full(params) * dw_full(params)
avail <- convolve_pred_kernel(params, prey)
# Add the interaction with the resource and the search volume to get the
# resource part of the encounter rate
encounter_resource <- avail * species_params(params)$interaction_resource *
    search_vol(params)
